ai.description: Raorchestes charius is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum, distinct dark interorbital band, and yellow-spotted flanks. It features a blunt snout and granular skin on the belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes charius* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or golden-yellow groin and hidden surfaces of the thighs, which contrast sharply with its body.
ai.habitat: Raorchestes charius inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Raorchestes charius is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden in dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects among the forest undergrowth.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes charius* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in vegetation or tree hollows.
ai.distributionRemarks: Raorchestes charius is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting the high-altitude evergreen forests of Karnataka and Kerala.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes charius* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude shola forests.
